The "extracted / needsValidation / error" handles map onto that shape via fan-out from the success port and per-script use of `$vars.{ixpNode}.output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields[…]` (the canonical access path) vs `$vars.{ixpNode}.error`. Assertions accept any valid wiring that yields three named script nodes plus a passing flow validate.
Validate-only: no `uip maestro flow debug`.

62	
63	1. **Always validate node types against the registry before building.** Use `registry search`/`list` for discovery and `registry get` for detailed metadata and definitions.
64	2. **ALWAYS follow the relevant plugin in [plugins/](references/plugins/) for every node type.** Each plugin has a `planning.md` (when to use, selection heuristics, ports) and `impl.md` (registry validation, JSON structure, CLI commands, configuration, debug). For connector nodes, the [connector](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) plugin covers connection binding, enriched metadata, and field resolution — required before building. Without this, node configuration will be wrong — errors that `flow validate` does not catch.
65	3. **Read the relevant Integration Service reference doc before any `uip is ...` call.** Two non-overlapping contracts:
66	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md) before any `uip is connections ...` call.** Applies to every connector activity, connector trigger, and managed HTTP node in connected mode. 67	   - **Read [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md](../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md) before any `uip is resources run ...` call.** Applies to every reference-field lookup (Slack user IDs, Jira project keys, Outlook folder IDs, etc.). Plugin files cover node-specific configuration that follows connection binding: [connector/impl.md](references/plugins/connector/impl.md), [connector-trigger/impl.md](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md), [http/impl-connector.md](references/plugins/http/impl-connector.md).
68	4. **Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` only** — other generated files (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`, `package-descriptor.json`) are managed by the CLI and may be overwritten. To declare flow inputs/outputs, add variables in the `.flow` file (see [shared/file-format.md](../shared/file-format.md)).
69	5. **`targetPort` is required on every edge** — `validate` rejects edges without it.
70	6. **Every node type needs a `definitions` entry** — copy from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type>` output. Never hand-write definitions. The definition is the sole source for BPMN type (`model.type`), serviceType, event definitions, and binding/context templates — none of that belongs on the instance.
71	7. **Script nodes must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. `scripts/lint_jint.py <flow>` checks this alongside the unsupported-construct scan.
72	8. **Validate once at the end** — run `uip maestro flow validate` only after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual node add or edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid. Run `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py <ProjectName>.flow` in the same step: it reports the structural defects `validate` does not catch (see [diagnose/failure-modes.md](../diagnose/references/failure-modes.md)).
73	9. **Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file** — there are no CLI commands for variable management. Use `Edit` to add/remove/update entries in the `variables` section of the `.flow` file, or `scripts/flow_edit.py add-variable | add-output-mapping | add-variable-update` for the documented shapes. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md).
74	10. **Every `out` variable must be mapped on every reachable End node** — missing output mappings cause runtime errors. See [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md). `scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` lists the unmapped pairs.
75	11. **`=js:` prefix is REQUIRED on every `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` reference in a value field** — not on condition expressions (decision, switch, HTTP branch), which are auto-evaluated as JS. Without it, the BPMN runtime sees a literal string and `flow validate` fails with MST-9107. See [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the canonical rule and per-node-type field reference, and [shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the expression system.
76	12. **Always run `flow format` after edits** — `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` is the canonical layout step. Format arranges nodes horizontally, sets each node's `size` by its canvas shape (inline agents → 288×96, containers → 560×320, everything else → 96×96), and recurses into subflows (`subflows[<id>].layout`). Skipping format is the most common cause of misshapen nodes in Studio Web.
77	13. **Don't hand-write `layout.nodes` or `subflows[<id>].layout`** — these are owned by `flow format`. When authoring nodes, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save. Sticky notes (`type: "stickyNote"`) are the one exception — format preserves their custom size and position. See [shared/file-format.md — Layout](../shared/file-format.md#layout).
78	14. **Every data-producing node MUST have a matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — this is what makes `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` resolve.** The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput>` declarations the runtime needs. The instance `outputs` block is **only** consumed by BPMN serialization on end-style nodes (to map workflow-level `out` variables); for action / trigger nodes it is documentation, not behavior. Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). **Always run `uip maestro flow format` after structural edits — it regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`** (matching what `uip maestro flow node add` and the canvas save path do), so this becomes self-healing as long as you `format`. See [shared/file-format.md — Node outputs](../shared/file-format.md#node-outputs).
79	15. **Node instances have no `model` block** — BPMN type, serviceType, version, event definitions, and binding/context templates live in the node's **definition** (in the top-level `definitions[]` array, copied verbatim from `registry get`). The runtime hydrates these from the definition at serialization time. Instance-specific identity fields live under `inputs`: `entryPointId`, `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers), `color`/`content` (sticky notes), and `source` (every inline-agent-related node — both `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node use `inputs.source = <UUID>`; their definitions declare `model.source: true` and flow-core hoists onto the instance).
80	16. **Error handling is off by default — never enable it on a node that handles no stated failure.** (`scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports a flag with no handler, and an error edge that rejoins the happy path or shares the success terminal — whether a node *should* handle a failure is a requirements call.) Leave `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` unset and add no `error` edge unless the requirements say what should happen when that node fails ("if the call fails…", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts"). An unhandled failure must fault the flow. When you do wire an `error` edge, it must reach a terminal the caller can distinguish from success — never the next happy-path node or the success End node. Without this, a failed run reports success. See [shared/file-format.md — Implicit error port on action nodes](../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
81	17. **Never invent the business meaning or format of a named output — elicit it.** When a request names an output (`caseKey`, `severity`, `status`, `ticketId`, …) but does not define how its value is derived, treat that as a business decision, not a coding choice — whether an identifier passes through unchanged or is reformatted (prefixed, combined, recomputed) is the user's rule to state, not yours to guess. Ask before building ([SKILL.md rule #5](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) — dropdown + "Something else"), or state your assumption explicitly and get confirmation. A guessed format produces a flow that passes `flow validate` yet returns the wrong value at runtime — the validator checks structure, never business correctness.

7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10	
11	**Plan when:**
12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach

16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))
18	- The flow is a straightforward linear pipeline (trigger → action → action → end)
19	- The user has already described the exact topology they want

21	### Examples
22	
23	**Plan:** "Build a flow that receives a Jira ticket, classifies it with an AI agent, routes urgent tickets to Slack and non-urgent to a queue, and logs everything to a Google Sheet."

25

37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |

47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.

52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.

268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.

272	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
273	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
274	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.

276	
277	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. 278	
279	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
280	
281	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
282	
283	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
284	
285	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
286	|---|---|---|
287	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
288	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
289	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
290	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
291	
292	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
293	
294	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
295	
296	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
297	
298	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
299	
300	**Or skip the anchoring problem:** `scripts/flow_edit.py` and `scripts/flow_compose.py` parse the file and rewrite the arrays directly, so no `old_string` has to be unique. One call per node, edge, variable, or composite rewrite — see [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) for the per-operation flags. `Edit` remains the right tool for a small in-place value change you want to show as a diff.
301	
302	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
303	
304	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

2	
3	IxP Extraction nodes invoke a published UiPath Intelligent eXtraction Platform (IxP) model. They are tenant-specific resources with pattern `uipath.ixp.{sanitized-modelName}.{sanitized-fullyQualifiedName}`.
4	
5	Sanitization rule (applied to both tail segments, in this order):
6	
7	1. Lowercase.
8	2. Replace runs of any character outside `[a-z0-9]` with a single `-`. Slashes, spaces, underscores, and runs of dashes (e.g. `---`) all collapse to a single `-`. Dots in the FQN are NOT preserved — they also collapse to `-`.
9	
10	The dot in `uipath.ixp.{model}.{fqn}` is the segment separator the registry adds *after* sanitizing each tail segment, not part of the sanitization itself.
11	
12	Examples (verified against the live registry):
13	
14	- `"birth_certificates_oob-6252526a-ixp"` + FQN `Shared/birth_certificates_oob-6252526a-ixp` → `uipath.ixp.birth-certificates-oob-6252526a-ixp.shared-birth-certificates-oob-6252526a-ixp` (underscores and slash both → `-`).
15	- `"idp-benchmark---invoices-c735405a-ixp"` + FQN `Shared/idp-benchmark---invoices-c735405a-ixp` → `uipath.ixp.idp-benchmark-invoices-c735405a-ixp.shared-idp-benchmark-invoices-c735405a-ixp` (run of `---` → single `-`).

114	
115	The IxP node instance carries `inputs` and `outputs` — and **no top-level `model` block**. 117	### Build procedure — copy from `registry get`, do not construct from memory
118	
119	The IxP node instance is **derived from the registry response**, not authored from scratch. Any IxP node built from training-data recall will hit at least one of: missing `inputs.model` (canvas crash), missing `outputs.error` (`flow validate` exits 1), legacy forbidden fields (silent schema drift).

130	| --- | --- | --- |

132	| `inputs.model.modelName` | `Data.Node.inputDefaults.model.modelName`, **but when that is `null`/empty, use `Data.Node.inputDefaults.model.modelDisplayName`** | **YES** — `null`/empty → `flow validate` fails (`ixp-node`: must be a non-empty string) |

134	| `inputs.projectName` | `Data.Node.inputDefaults.projectName` | YES |
135	| `inputs.folderKey` | `Data.Node.inputDefaults.folderKey` | YES |
136	| `inputs.folderName` | `Data.Node.inputDefaults.folderName` | YES |
137	| `inputs.versionTag` | `""` (empty string unless pinning a version) | YES |
138	| `inputs.pageRange` | `""` (empty string for full document) | YES |
139	| `inputs.fileRef` | `"=js:$vars.<upstream>.output.<field>"` — the file/attachment OBJECT itself, never its `.ID` (author this) | YES |
140	| `outputs.output` | the four-field literal below (no `registry get` lookup needed) | **YES** — missing → `flow validate` fails |

203	### Authoring rules
204	
205	1. **`inputs.model` MUST be present and MUST be copied from `Data.Node.inputDefaults.model`.** Copy the blob verbatim — do not abbreviate, do not omit fields, do not invent fields that aren't there. The current deployment-node blob is `{ id, modelName, modelDisplayName, folderKey, folderName, folderPath, description }`; source every field from the actual `registry get` response, not from memory (older docs showed `fullyQualifiedName` / `kind` / `type` / `detailsUrl` / `async*` fields — these are NOT present on deployment nodes; do not add them). The `schema-definition` form section binds `inputs.model` to the `ixp-model-taxonomy` custom component, which destructures `modelName` and `folderKey` out of it. If `inputs.model` is undefined, clicking the node in Studio Web crashes the property panel with `Cannot destructure property 'modelName' of 't' as it is undefined` — and `flow validate` fails on it too (`ixp-node`: `inputs.model must be an object with non-empty string modelName and folderKey`).
206	   - **`inputs.model.modelName` MUST be a non-empty string.** For many published/OOB deployments `inputDefaults.model.modelName` comes back `null`, with the name carried in `inputDefaults.model.modelDisplayName` instead. When `modelName` is `null`/empty, set `inputs.model.modelName` to `modelDisplayName`. This is NOT synthesis — `modelDisplayName` is the model's own name from the same blob (and matches the flat `inputDefaults.modelName`). The `ixp-node` validator rejects a `null`/empty `inputs.model.modelName` (`flow validate` fails), and Studio Web crashes on it.
207	2. **Flat mirrors stay alongside `inputs.model`.** `modelName`, `projectName`, `folderKey`, `folderName` are surfaced as disabled text fields in the `ixp-model` form section and are read directly from `inputs.*`, not from `inputs.model.*`.
208	3. **`fileRef` is the only schema-required input** (`inputDefinition.required: ["fileRef"]`). Use `=js:$vars.<upstream>.output.<field>` per Critical Rule #13. The upstream `<field>` variable MUST be declared `type: "file"` — `type: "object"` breaks attachment binding and faults extraction even when the `fileRef` expression itself is correct. See [Wiring `fileRef`](#wiring-fileref--file-variable-bound-to-the-trigger).
209	4. **`outputs.output` AND `outputs.error` MUST both be present** — copy the fixed four-field literals from [Final shape](#final-shape); they are identical for every IxP node and need no `registry get` lookup. **`flow validate` hard-fails on the omission** — `ixp-node` emits `[nodes[<nodeId>].outputs.output] outputs.output must be present on the instance`, and the matching error for `outputs.error`.
210	5. **No top-level `model` on the instance.** Studio Web–authored .flow files never carry one; the BPMN-format `model` envelope (with `context`, `version`, `inputs`, `outputs`) is emitted at serialize time only.
211	6. **`inputs` MUST NOT contain `digitizationMode`, `documentTaxonomy`, `attachmentId`, `fileName`, or `mimeType`.** These five fields were on a prior schema and have been removed from the standalone IxP node. Including them is the most common training-data-recall mistake. The serializer defaults `digitizationMode` to `fileUpload` internally — there is no scenario where you should set it on the instance.
212	7. **Every edge carries all five keys** — `id`, `sourceNodeId`, `sourcePort`, `targetNodeId`, `targetPort`. The node-reference keys are `sourceNodeId` / `targetNodeId`, not `source` / `target`. Port names are under [Registry Validation](#registry-validation).
213	
214	The `definitions[]` entry is copied verbatim from `registry get` (`Data.Node`) — every key, including `sortOrder`, which the schema requires on each definition. Critical Rule #7 applies unchanged.
215	
216	> **`uip maestro flow validate` enforces the Authoring rules above** via the `ixp-node` validator. Failures surface as `severity: "error"` issues with `path` like `nodes[<nodeId>].inputs.model` and a self-contained `message` describing the violation — fix the `.flow` file, not the validator. A common failure is `inputs.model must be an object with non-empty string modelName and folderKey` — this fires when `inputDefaults.model.modelName` was `null` and copied through verbatim; fix it by setting `inputs.model.modelName` from `inputDefaults.model.modelDisplayName` (Authoring rule #1), not by relaxing the validator. The registry's `inputDefinition.properties` is the schema of the property catalog, not a license to override the rules: `digitizationMode`, `documentTaxonomy`, `attachmentId`, `fileName`, and `mimeType` are NOT returned by `registry get` and must not be set on the instance.

231	      "direction": "in",
232	      "type": "file",
233	      "triggerNodeId": "start"

251	
252	`inputDefinition.properties.attachment` accepts `{ ID, FullName, MimeType, Metadata }` for flows that consume Orchestrator job attachments. 254	## Accessing Output
255	
256	The extraction result is stored at `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. The IxP node's BPMN serializer maps the extraction service's `result` field directly to this variable (`source: '=result'`), so **the `result` wrapper is stripped** — `output` IS the extraction-result object, with no further wrapping.
257	
258	Top-level keys of `$vars.{nodeId}.output`:
259	
260	- `ExtractionResult` — `{ DocumentId, ResultsVersion, ResultsDocument }`. `ResultsDocument.Fields[]` carries the trained model's extracted values; `ResultsDocument.Tables[]` carries tabular extractions.
261	- `ExtractorPayloads` — provider-specific raw payloads.
262	- `BusinessrulesResults[]` — business-rule evaluation results, when configured.
263	
264	Each `Fields[]` element is shaped:
265	
266	```json
267	{
268	  "FieldId": "string",
269	  "FieldName": "string",
270	  "FieldType": "string",
271	  "IsMissing": false,
272	  "Values": ["string"],
273	  "Confidence": 95
274	}
275	```
276	
277	Read field values via `find` against `FieldName`, then index into `Values[]`:
278	
279	```javascript
280	// In a Script node after the IxP node
281	const fields = $vars.extractInvoiceFields.output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields || [];
282	const total = fields.find(f => f.FieldName === 'invoiceTotal')?.Values?.[0];
283	const vendor = fields.find(f => f.FieldName === 'vendor')?.Values?.[0];
284	return { total, vendor };
285	```
286	
287	Sibling error variable: `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — populated when extraction fails *and* the `error` port is wired (`supportsErrorHandling: true`). Mapped from the service response's `Error` field (`source: '=Error'`).
288	
289	### Wrong shapes the agent tends to invent
290	
291	These all pass `flow validate` and fail silently at runtime:
292	
293	- **Wrong:** `output.result.ExtractionResult.…` — there is no `result` wrapper at runtime; `=result` strips it before the value is assigned to `output`.
294	- **Wrong:** `output.<fieldName>` flat — extracted fields are not top-level properties of `output`; they live under `output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields[]` and are keyed by `FieldName`.
295	- **Wrong:** `output.ExtractionResult.Fields` — `Fields[]` is two levels under `ExtractionResult` (`output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields`), not one.
296	
297	Studio Web's variable picker renders `output.ExtractionResult` as opaque and does NOT surface the nested `ResultsDocument.Fields[]` shape. The path above is the source of truth — copy it from this doc, not from picker autocomplete or `outputDefinition.output.schema` (the registry schema describes the pre-`=result` wrapper, not the runtime variable).
298	
299	### Trained-model field taxonomy
300	
301	The `FieldName` values present in `ResultsDocument.Fields[]` depend on the trained IxP model's taxonomy and are NOT exposed through `uip maestro flow registry get` (the registry's `outputDefinition.output.schema` describes the wrapper envelope shape, not the per-model trained fields). Get them from the deployment:
302	
303	```bash
304	uip ixp deployments get-taxonomy --folder-key <folderKey> "<modelName>" --output json
305	```
306	
307	Both args come from the `registry get` response you already fetched in [Build procedure](#build-procedure--copy-from-registry-get-do-not-construct-from-memory): `--folder-key` ← `Data.Node.inputDefaults.folderKey`; `<modelName>` (positional) ← `Data.Node.inputDefaults.modelName`. No additional discovery step. Requires `uip login`; the command uses the user Bearer to call the same DU-App route that Studio Web's "Schema definition" panel uses.
308	
309	Response shape:
310	
311	```json
312	{
313	  "documentTaxonomy": {
314	    "documentTypes": [
315	      {
316	        "fields": [
317	          {
318	            "fieldId": "string",
319	            "fieldName": "string",
320	            "type": "Text",
321	            "components": []
322	          }
323	        ]
324	      }
325	    ]
326	  }
327	}
328	```
329	
330	`type` is one of `Text`, `Date`, `Number`, `Set`, `FieldGroup`. `components[]` is populated only when `type` is `FieldGroup` and carries sub-fields with the same shape recursively.
331	
332	**camelCase → PascalCase translation.** The taxonomy response uses `fieldName` (camelCase); runtime `Fields[]` elements use `FieldName` (PascalCase). The string *contents* match — design-time `"Birth Date"` is `FieldName: "Birth Date"` at runtime — but the wrapper key changes case. Translate the key, not the value, when going from `get-taxonomy` output to runtime `Fields[].FieldName` lookups.
333	
334	Agent call sequence:
335	
336	1. `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp" --output json` — list IxP nodes.
337	2. `uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --output json` — read `Data.Node.inputDefaults.{folderKey, modelName}` (already done as part of [Build procedure](#build-procedure--copy-from-registry-get-do-not-construct-from-memory)).
338	3. `uip ixp deployments get-taxonomy --folder-key <folderKey> "<modelName>" --output json` — read `documentTaxonomy.documentTypes[].fields[].fieldName`.
339	4. Author downstream consumers with `$vars.<id>.output.ExtractionResult.ResultsDocument.Fields.find(f => f.FieldName === '<fieldName from step 3>')?.Values?.[0]`.
340	
341	If the command fails (login expired, deployment not yet published, transient failure), fall back to defensive `find`-by-`FieldName` patterns with assumed field names and surface the assumptions to the user under **Open Questions**. Do NOT substitute a one-off extraction or IxP-product-UI inspection in the agent loop — `get-taxonomy` is the agent-loop path.

351	
352	Trigger: `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp"` returns `Data: []`, OR the only matches are `uipath.agent.resource.tool.ixp.*` (agent-tool variant — not a flow extraction node).
353	
354	Action: insert a `core.logic.mock` placeholder via Direct JSON edit and stop. Do not iterate on registry searches.
355	
356	1. Fetch the definition: `uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.mock --output json`. Copy `Data.Node` verbatim into `definitions[]` if not already present.
357	2. Add a node to `nodes[]` with a stable id (e.g. `extractContractFieldsMock`), `type: "core.logic.mock"`, and a `display.label` whose **leading phrase** describes the work in the user's domain (e.g. `Extract Contract Fields`) rather than the underlying technology (`IxP Extraction`, `Run IxP`). The parenthetical may name IxP — e.g. `Extract Contract Fields (mock — IxP model not yet published)`.
358	3. Add a `layout.nodes` entry at `position: { x: 400, y: 144 }`, size `96x96`.

360	5. **Wire downstream consumers against the mock with `$vars` references, not static values.** Scripts, decisions, and end-node mappings that follow the mock MUST reference `$vars.{mockNodeId}.output` (the mock's only port) instead of hard-coded returns. Example: a script that summarises the (future) extraction writes `return { vendor: $vars.extractInvoiceFieldsMock.output.vendorName };`, not `return { ok: "OK" };`. This keeps the **node-graph** swap-ready — node IDs, edge shapes, and the `output` port name stay intact when the mock is replaced. **Field-access paths inside downstream scripts WILL need rewriting at swap time** — the real IxP `output` is shaped as `{ ExtractionResult: { ResultsDocument: { Fields: [...] } } }` (see [Accessing Output](#accessing-output)), so flat-field accessors against the mock become structured `Fields.find(f => f.FieldName === '<name>')?.Values?.[0]` lookups against the real node. Surface the post-swap rewrite as a follow-up under **Open Questions**.
361	6. Run `uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json` once after all edits complete.
362	
363	Surface the missing model in the **Open Questions** section of the architectural plan: the user must train and publish the IxP extraction model via the IxP product before the flow can run. After publishing, follow the [mock replacement procedure](../../editing-operations-json.md#replace-a-mock-with-a-real-resource-node) to swap the mock for the real IxP node.

369	## Debug
370	
371	| Error | Cause | Fix |
372	| --- | --- | --- |
373	| Node type not found in registry | Model not published, or registry cache stale | Run `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
374	| `model.context` rejected by runtime | `folderKey` or `modelName` missing from `inputs` (the context array is built from these) | Confirm `inputs.modelName` and `inputs.folderKey` are populated. |

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	8. **Never name a variable `aggregate`** — reserved host global. On any `Identifier 'X' has already been declared`, rename `X`.
43	
44	**Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py <ProjectName>.flow` checks rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 above (plus the wider unsupported-construct list) across every script node and `=js:` expression in the file. The 30-second timeout is a runtime property and is not statically checkable.
45	
46	## Common patterns
47	
48	### Transform and return
49	
50	```javascript
51	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
52	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
53	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
54	```
55	
56	### Build a payload for a downstream node
57	
58	```javascript
59	return {
60	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
61	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
62	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
63	};
64	```
65	
66	### Error check from upstream
67	
68	```javascript
69	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
70	if (error) {
71	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
72	}
73	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
74	```
75	
76	### Reading a file-typed variable
77	
78	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
79	
80	```javascript
81	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
82	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
83	```
84	
85	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
86	
87	## Debug
88	
89	| Error | Cause | Fix |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
91	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
92	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
93	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
94	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
95	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
96	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
97	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
98	| `[300501] Error invoking script task` with `Unexpected token` | Malformed JavaScript — `flow validate` does not parse script bodies, so syntax errors surface only at runtime. Common slip: one missing `)` in chained `(((a \|\| {}).b \|\| {}).c \|\| [])` guards | Balance parentheses; check with `node -e "new Function(<script>)"` before validate |
99	| `Identifier 'X' has already been declared` | `X` collides with a runtime-injected global (known: `aggregate`) | Rename `X` (e.g. `agg`) |

1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 **Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py ` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`. 542 543 --- 544 545 ## Scoping Rules 546 547 ### Node Output Availability 548 549 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 550 551 ### Loop Scope 552 553 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 554 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 555 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 556 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 557 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 558 559 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 560 561 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 562 563 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 564 565 ### Subflow Scope 566 567 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 568 569 --- 570 571 ## Variable Management via CLI 572 573 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 574 575 ### Adding a workflow input variable 576 577 1. Open `.flow` 578 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 579 3. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 599 600 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 601 602 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 603 604 ```json 605 "outputs": { 606 "result": { 607 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 608 } 609 } 610 ``` 611 612 --- 613 614 ## Complete Example 615 616 A flow with input, state, and output 39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." 41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.

44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->

47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.

93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.

137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):

192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — without rewriting anything; `uip maestro flow format` remains the fix.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).

230	## Edge — both ports required
231	
232	```json
233	{
234	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
235	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
236	  "sourcePort": "output",
237	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
238	  "targetPort": "input"
239	}
240	```
241	
242	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
245	>
246	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.

Depending on CLI/plugin version, that object may appear at `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`. Do not write definitions by hand — always pull from the registry to ensure schema compliance.

284	## Standard ports by node type
285	
286	| Node type | Source ports (outgoing) | Target ports (incoming) |
287	|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
288	| `core.trigger.manual` | `output` | — |
289	| `core.action.script` | `success`, `error` | `input` |
290	| `core.action.http.v2` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic) | `input` |
291	| `core.action.transform` | `output`, `error` | `input` |
292	| `core.logic.decision` | `true`, `false` | `input` |
293	| `core.logic.switch` | `case-{id}` (dynamic), `default` | `input` |
294	| `core.logic.loop` | `success`, `output` | `input`, `loopBack` |
295	| `core.logic.merge` | `output` | `input` |
296	| `core.control.end` | — | `input` |
297	| `core.logic.terminate` | — | `input` |

299	Connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes follow the same pattern as the generic action nodes above: a primary source port plus an implicit `error` port.
300	
301	Verify exact ports for any node type:
302	```bash
303	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
304	# Look at Data.Node.handleConfiguration[].handles[].id
305	# Also check Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling — see "Implicit error port" below
306	```
307	
308	## Implicit error port on action nodes
309	
310	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
311	
312	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
313	
314	### Default: off — enable only for a failure the flow actually handles
315	
316	`inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is **opt-in, and stays off unless the requirements name a failure fallback.** Turning it on suppresses the node's fault: the node returns instead of faulting and execution continues. Enable it only when both hold:
317	
318	1. The requirements state what should happen when this node fails ("if the call fails, …", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts") — **and**
319	2. You wire the node's `error` port to a handler that produces an outcome distinguishable from success.
320	
321	Never set the flag on a node that has no outgoing `error` edge — it suppresses the fault with nothing to catch it, converting a real failure into a run that reports success. Let the CLI own the flag: `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set it from the error edges actually present. If you find the flag on a node with no error edge, remove it.
322	
323	### Do not swallow the failure
324	
325	An `error` edge must not rejoin the happy path. When it does, every failure walks the success route and the run reports `Completed` while the work never happened — the flow "always looks successful."
326	
327	| | Error-path target | Result |
328	| --- | --- | --- |
329	| ✗ | The next node on the happy path | Failure is invisible; downstream nodes run on missing data |
330	| ✗ | The same End node the success path reaches | Success path's output mappings run against the failed node's empty output |
331	| ✓ | A **distinct** End node mapping an error/status `out` variable | Caller can tell failure from success |
332	| ✓ | `core.logic.terminate` | Aborts the flow when recovery is impossible — see [terminate/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/terminate/impl.md) |
333	| ✓ | A recovery branch that rejoins **only after obtaining valid data** — a retry that succeeded, or a fallback source that returned data | Downstream runs on real data, not on the failed node's empty output |
334	
335	```text
336	Trigger -> HTTP Request
337	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
338	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", message from $vars.httpCall.error)
339	```
340	
341	### When the error port fires
342	
343	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
344	- Request timeouts
345	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
346	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
347	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
348	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
349	
350	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`. **That is the correct default, not a defect to design around** — a faulted run is visible to the operator; a swallowed failure is not. Only trade the fault for an error path when the requirements say what that path should do.
351	
352	### Wiring the error port
353	
354	```bash
355	# Confirm the node supports error handling
356	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
357	
358	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
359	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
360	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
361	```
362	
363	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically — only for nodes that have an error edge. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself **on those nodes only**:
364	
365	```json
366	{
367	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
368	  "inputs": {
369	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
370	  }
371	}
372	```
373	
374	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
375	
376	### Error port vs other branching
377	
378	| Mechanism | When to use |
379	| --- | --- |
380	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
381	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
382	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
383	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |
